content:
After two candidate versions, Apple officially launched macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, and macOS 27.0.1 today. Below are the details.

macOS 27.0.1, macOS 26.7.1 and macOS 15.8.1 are now available

After two candidate versions, Apple is officially pushing macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 to users, along with macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, the first update following the earlier release of macOS 27 this month.

Today's launch comes exactly one week after Apple pushed out the second round of candidate versions last week, with those candidates then rolled out to the general public the following day.

Apple's release notes for the candidate versions only mentioned standard security fixes and performance improvements, but recent updates have contained important security patches, many of which addressed vulnerabilities discovered with the help of AI tools.

Apple has even confirmed that the growing capabilities of AI tools are affecting its security update cycle. Back in June, the company said it had pushed out fixes earlier than originally planned for the 26.6 release, because AI can speed up the development of malicious hacking tools, and Apple did not want there to be too long a gap between publicly releasing the fixes and getting them installed by users.

Apple is expected to publish the security details for macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 within the next few hours, and we will report on the key points at that time.

Update, 1:59 p.m. ET: Apple said macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate "has no published CVE entries," but noted that macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 have addressed the following issues:

CoreGraphics Available for: macOS Sequoia Impact: Processing a specially crafted malicious file could lead to arbitrary code execution. Apple is aware of a report indicating that this issue may have been exploited in extremely sophisticated attacks targeting specific individuals on devices running a version of iOS that is not the latest. Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed by improving bounds checking. CVE-2026-86950: Meta Product Security

Here are the build numbers for today's macOS releases:

  • macOS Sequoia 15.8: 24H32
  • macOS Tahoe 26.7.1: 25G241
  • macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate: 26A5434

Have you spotted anything new in this release? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
